query: For lightweight high-entropy alloys intended for weight-critical aerospace and rail-transport applications, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain their ability—or inability—to combine low density with mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance? Specify an unnamed controlled comparison that would test the hypothesis, the observations predicted relative to a baseline alloy, the conditions under which the hypothesis should cease to hold, the existing observations that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In lightweight, Al- and Ti-rich body-centred-cubic (BCC) high-entropy alloys (HEAs), nanometre-scale short-range chemical ordering (SRC) of Al/Ti-enriched clusters forms during moderate-temperature ageing. 1) The SRC locally increases lattice friction stress and acts as strong, thermally stable obstacles to dislocation glide, thereby raising yield strength. 2) The same SRC drives rapid, selective outward diffusion of Al (and Ti) during exposure to air, producing a continuous, adherent Al2O3/TiO2 mixed scale that suppresses further oxidation and corrosion. If the SRC is erased by full homogenisation, both strengthening and oxidation resistance degrade while density stays unchanged. Thus, the joint occurrence of SRC—not merely high configurational entropy—mechanistically enables the unusual combination of low density, high strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: Al-Ti-(Cr,V) lightweight BCC high-entropy alloy solidified and hot-forged to a single-phase supersaturated solid solution without prior ageing; density ≈ 5 g cm⁻³.
generation.intervention: Thermomechanical treatment that induces and preserves Al/Ti-rich short-range chemical ordering (e.g., 0.7 T_m ageing for 4 h) versus a control treatment that fully homogenises the alloy at >0.9 T_m followed by rapid quench to suppress SRC.
generation.conditions: Tests conducted at 25 °C to 800 °C in laboratory air (for oxidation) and inert atmosphere (for mechanical tests). Effect expected as long as SRC is stable; it should vanish above ~0.8 T_m where ordering dissolves.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanometre-scale Al/Ti-enriched short-range ordered clusters embedded in a BCC high-entropy solid solution.
generation.mechanism: SRC produce local lattice distortions that raise the Peierls barrier to dislocation motion (solid-solution⁄order strengthening) and create rapid diffusion paths for Al/Ti toward the surface, forming a protective, slow-growing oxide scale; removal of SRC eliminates these effects.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared with the homogenised baseline: (a) 25–40 % higher yield strength and 20–30 % higher 0.2 % proof stress at 600 °C; (b) 40–60 % lower mass gain after 100 h oxidation at 800 °C; (c) similar density within ±1 %; (d) if homogenised sample is re-aged to restore SRC, strength and oxidation resistance should recover.
generation.baseline: Same alloy composition fully homogenised (>0.9 T_m, 2 h, water-quenched) to minimise SRC before testing.
generation.boundary: Hypothesis ceases to hold if: 1) ageing temperature exceeds ∼0.8 T_m long enough to dissolve SRC; 2) alloy compositions that do not form Al/Ti-rich clusters (e.g., lacking Al) are tested; 3) environments that form volatile oxides (e.g., chlorine-rich) where alumina scale is unstable.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of SRC contribution to oxidation resistance is estimated; direct quantification of Al/Ti flux during scale formation is lacking. Competing effects from oxide-dispersion, grain size or long-range ordering may also influence results.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three lots of the same Al-Ti-(Cr,V) HEA bar stock: (1) SRC-rich (aged 0.7 T_m, 4 h), (2) SRC-free (homogenised 0.95 T_m, 2 h, water-quenched), (3) Re-aged after homogenisation. Confirm SRC presence/absence with atom-probe tomography and diffuse-scattering TEM. Measure: (i) tensile yield strength at 25 °C and 600 °C; (ii) weight gain and scale morphology after isothermal oxidation in air at 800 °C for 100 h; (iii) Vickers microhardness cross-sections below the oxide.
measurements: Atom-probe compositional maps (SRC fraction, cluster size)
Oxide scale thickness and composition by SEM/EDS
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If SRC-free samples show equal or higher high-temperature yield strength OR equal or lower oxidation mass gain compared with SRC-rich samples (outside experimental error of ±5 %), the hypothesis is falsified.
